summary: Validates list API responses at the boundary so an unexpected non-array payload logs an actionable diagnostic and degrades to an empty list instead of throwing an opaque runtime TypeError.
userImpact: A list endpoint returning a non-array payload (an error envelope, an object, or a string) now renders an empty list instead of crashing the view with `TypeError: ... is not a function`.

Developers get a console diagnostic naming the request and describing the payload shape, so API contract mismatches, missing endpoints, and auth or configuration problems are identifiable without hand-instrumenting the code.
configuration: No configuration or settings changes. The Email Configurations admin page is touched only by the list-response validation refactor (its list fetch now routes through `fetchList`); operators need take no action and no environment variables, settings, or config bundles change.

changes: Adds `expectArray(value, context)` and `fetchList<T>(url, params?, options?, context?)` to `@enterpriseglue/frontend-host` `shared/api`; the existing `apiClient` surface is unchanged and `fetchList` is a drop-in for `apiClient.get<T[]>(...)`.

security: Unexpected payloads are described by type and key names in all environments; the full payload body is logged only in development builds, so production logs do not capture unexpected response contents.
knownLimitations: Coverage is limited to GET list endpoints routed through `fetchList`; non-array `POST` responses and array data arriving via WebSocket/SSE or plugin bridges are not yet guarded, though `expectArray` is exported for incremental reuse.
rollback: Redeploy the previous frontend image or `@enterpriseglue/frontend-host` package; no configuration or database rollback is required.
validation: Full frontend unit suite (`vitest --run`) passes with new tests covering `expectArray` (arrays, null/undefined, error envelopes, string and object payloads) and `fetchList` (array pass-through, non-array coercion with logged context, argument forwarding).
`@enterpriseglue/frontend-host` typecheck (`tsc -p tsconfig.build.json --noEmit`) and repository ESLint (`--max-warnings=0`) are clean over the changed files.
